notices.short_title: Defensive Driving Services
notices.description:
DCAS is requesting to extend the contract for 18 months from February 28, 2026, to August 27, 2027 to continue defensive driving services with National Traffic Safety Institute Corporation (NTSI) through the Negotiated Acquisition Extension procurement method pursuant to §3-04(b)(2)(iii) of the Procurement Policy Board Rules.

The cost of this NAE will be $375,000.00. This extension is needed while DCAS works on an RFP for a new contract. DCAS is currently in the evaluation process to award a vendor.

The term of the original contract was March 1, 2017, through February 28, 2020.

DCAS renewed the contract CT1856 20205401621 for a period of 3 years term from February 29, 2020 through February 27, 2023.

DCAS has exercised the 1-year ACCO extension, from February 28, 2023 through February 27, 2024. DCAS has exercised the first NAE(CT120248806088) from February 28, 2024 through February 27, 2025.

DCAS has exercised the second NAE (CTI 20258807034) from February 28, 2025 through February 27, 2026 and will be utilizing a third NAE.
notices.plain: The Department of Citywide Administrative Services is extending its defensive driving services contract with National Traffic Safety Institute Corporation for 18 months, from Feb. 28, 2026, to Aug. 27, 2027, at a cost of $375,000, while the city seeks a new vendor.

notices.short_title: Integrated Commercial Hotels Program
notices.description:
The Department of Homeless Services (DHS') is seeking appropriately qualified contractors/vendors to contract for the provision of shelter services for families with children, adult families, and single adults who are temporarily housed in DHS contracted commercial hotels. The selected vendors will provide services as outlined in this RFP to assist clients with their daily needs and to help them move out of the shelter system as quickly as possible.

The mission of DHS is to prevent homelessness when possible and to provide short-term emergency shelter for individuals and families who have no other housing options available. DHS primarily meets this goal by providing services to clients in long-term contracted purpose-built shelters throughout the City. When there are not enough available shelter beds and units in traditional shelters, DHS temporarily uses commercial hotels to house clients while they transition to permanent housing.  

Over the last 15 years, DHS has faced numerous crises which have forced DHS to rely on commercial hotels to temporarily house clients. Long term DHS is committed to phasing out the use of commercial hotels. However, until such time th…
notices.plain: The Department of Homeless Services awarded Lantern Community Services Inc a $40,111,403 contract through a competitive proposal process to provide shelter and daily support services for families, adult families and single adults housed in city-contracted commercial hotels.

notices.short_title: Visual Inspections of Fire Standpipe and Sprinkler Systems
notices.description:
Through this RFQ series, NYCHA is administering a pilot procurement that introduces a streamlined bid submission and evaluation process, differing from NYCHA's conventional solicitation procedures. The pilot is intended to simplify the solicitation process for responding bidders while supporting NYCHA's ongoing efforts to strengthen competition, improve efficiency, and enhance transparency within the Authority's procurement process.

At the time of RFQ closing, responding bidders will only be required to submit the minimum documentation identified in the solicitation. Following bid opening, NYCHA will evaluate bid pricing and identify the apparent low bidder(s). During the evaluation process, NYCHA will request additional required documentation only from the apparent low bidder(s), or other bidder(s) as necessary, to complete the responsibility and responsiveness review. Bidders should not submit documents beyond the minimum required unless specifically requested by…

All Work designed, filed, performed and materials furnished under this Contract shall conform to the applicable requirements of the appropriate corresponding rules and regulations including without limitation the New York City Department of Buildings (DOB), New York City Fire Department (FDNY), and National Fire Protection Association Code 72 (NFPA 72).
